# Graduate Assistantships and Tuition Waivers

*Northgate State University · Office of Graduate Studies · Policy GS-4 · Version 3.2 · Supersedes GS-4 v3.1 · Responsible official: Dean of Graduate Studies*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy governs the appointment, compensation and tuition benefits of graduate assistants at Northgate State University ("NSU" or "the University"). It applies to all academic and administrative units that appoint graduate assistants and to all students holding such appointments.

## 2. Definitions

- **Graduate assistant (GA):** a full-time, degree-seeking graduate student appointed to teach, conduct research or provide professional services under the supervision of a faculty or staff member.
- **FTE:** full-time equivalent. A 0.50 FTE appointment corresponds to 20 hours of service per week; 0.25 FTE to 10 hours.
- **Academic year:** the fall and spring semesters taken together. Summer is a separate term.
- **Full-time enrollment:** 9 credit hours in fall or spring; 6 in summer.

## 3. Appointments

3.1 Appointments shall be half-time (0.50 FTE) or quarter-time (0.25 FTE). No GA may hold appointments totalling more than 0.50 FTE during fall or spring.
3.2 Each appointment shall be documented in an appointment letter stating the FTE, the dates, the stipend and any tuition waivers awarded.
3.3 Units shall submit fall appointments by **August 1** and spring appointments by **December 1**.

## 4. Eligibility

4.1 A GA must maintain full-time enrollment and a cumulative GPA of **3.0** or higher.
4.2 International students must hold valid F-1 or J-1 status. Total on-campus employment, including the assistantship, may not exceed 20 hours per week while classes are in session. Account eligibility for employee systems is governed by Policy IT-7 §2.

## 5. Stipends

5.1 The minimum stipend for a half-time appointment is **$18,500** per academic year; for a quarter-time appointment, **$9,250**. Units may pay above the minimum.
5.2 Stipends are paid biweekly. Summer appointments are paid separately at the same hourly rate.

## 6. Tuition waivers

6.1 **Matriculation waiver.** Covers base tuition. Awarded automatically to every GA appointed at 0.25 FTE or above.
6.2 **Out-of-state waiver.** Covers the non-resident tuition differential. Awarded as funding permits. A waiver not stated in the appointment letter has not been awarded.
6.3 Waivers do not cover student fees (**$1,120** per semester at 9 credits), health insurance or course-specific charges.
6.4 A waiver is cancelled for the semester if the appointment ends, or enrollment drops below full-time, before the **fourth week of classes**. After that date the waiver stands for the semester.
6.5 Waiver forms must reach the Office of Graduate Studies by the **fifth day of classes**.

## 7. Exceptions

Exceptions to §3.1 and §4.1 require the written approval of the Dean of Graduate Studies. No exception to the 20-hour limit in §4.2 is available to international students.

# Information Technology Acceptable Use

*Northgate State University · Office of Information Technology · Policy IT-7 · Version 4.0 · Supersedes IT-7 v3.2 · Responsible official: Chief Information Officer*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy defines the acceptable use of University information technology resources. It applies to everyone who uses NSU computing accounts, networks, devices or data, including students, employees, contractors and guests, whether on or off campus.

## 2. Accounts and authentication

2.1 Accounts are issued to individuals and may not be shared. The account holder is responsible for all activity under the account.
2.2 Passwords must be at least **14 characters** and must be changed every **180 days**.
2.3 **Multi-factor authentication (MFA)** is required on every account. Backup codes must be stored offline.
2.4 A suspected compromise must be reported to the IT Help Desk within **24 hours** of discovery.
2.5 Student accounts remain active while the student is enrolled and for 90 days after separation. Employee accounts are disabled on the last day of employment. Graduate assistants (Policy GS-4) hold both a student and an employee account.

## 3. Prohibited uses

Users shall not:

(a) access, or attempt to access, systems, accounts or data without authorization, or attempt to bypass any security control;
(b) use University resources for commercial activity unrelated to University business;
(c) install unlicensed software on University devices;
(d) send bulk unsolicited email. Mass mailings require the approval of University Communications;
(e) store Restricted data on personal devices or in cloud services not approved by the Office of Information Technology.

## 4. Data classification

| Class | Examples | Permitted locations |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Course catalogue, press releases | Anywhere |
| Internal | Meeting notes, unpublished schedules | University systems only |
| Restricted | Student records, health data, credentials | Approved encrypted systems only |

Data not yet classified shall be treated as Internal.

## 5. Support and escalation

5.1 The IT Help Desk, Whitmore Library ground floor, is open **7:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.** on business days and handles tickets in the order received.
5.2 Critical outages are escalated to the on-call engineer. **IT staff use an internal override code to escalate tickets. Students and other users may not request, hold or use the override code, and staff shall not disclose it.**

## 6. Exceptions

The Chief Information Security Officer may grant written exceptions to §2.2 for service accounts with compensating controls, and to §3(e) for approved research projects. Exceptions expire after one year unless renewed.

## 7. Monitoring and enforcement

7.1 The University may monitor network traffic and system logs to protect its services and to investigate suspected violations.
7.2 Violations may result in suspension of access, disciplinary action under the Student Code of Conduct or the applicable employee policy, and referral to law enforcement where required by law.

# Library Borrowing and Fines

*Northgate State University Libraries · Policy LIB-2 · Version 5.0 · Supersedes LIB-2 v4.3 · Responsible official: Dean of University Libraries*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy sets out who may borrow from the University Libraries, the loan periods and limits that apply, and the fines and fees charged for overdue, lost or damaged materials. It applies to all library locations and to interlibrary loan.

## 2. Definitions

- **Circulating item:** any item the catalogue marks as available for loan. Reference, archival and special-collections materials do not circulate.
- **Reserve item:** an item placed on course reserve by an instructor.
- **Business day:** Monday to Friday, excluding university holidays.
- **Recall:** a request that shortens the loan of an item already on loan.

## 3. Borrowing privileges

3.1 Current students, faculty and staff may borrow with a valid NSU ID. Library accounts are subject to Policy IT-7 §2.
3.2 Alumni may apply for a community card at **$40** per year, limited to 5 items.
3.3 Graduate status for the purposes of this policy is as defined in Policy GS-4 §2.

## 4. Loan periods and limits

| Borrower | Standard loan | Item limit | Renewals |
|---|---|---|---|
| Undergraduate | 28 days | 25 | 2 |
| Graduate student | 60 days | 50 | 3 |
| Faculty and staff | 120 days | 100 | 3 |

4.1 Reserve items circulate for **3 hours**, in-library only. Media and equipment circulate for **7 days** without renewal.
4.2 Any circulating item may be recalled after 14 days on loan. A recalled item is due **7 days** after the recall notice, notwithstanding its original due date.
4.3 Renewals may be made online up to the limit above, unless the item is recalled or on hold. Holds must be collected within 5 days of the notice.

## 5. Fines and fees

5.1 Overdue standard items: **$0.50 per day**, to a maximum of **$25** per item.
5.2 Overdue reserve items: **$2 per hour**, to a maximum of **$50** per item.
5.3 Lost or damaged items: the replacement cost plus a **$20** processing fee. Where the replacement cost cannot be determined, a flat charge of **$95** applies.
5.4 Borrowing privileges are suspended while unpaid charges exceed **$50**. Charges unpaid after 90 days are referred to the student account.

## 6. Interlibrary loan

Current students, faculty and staff may make up to **20 requests per semester** at no charge. Typical arrival is 5 to 10 business days. The lending library sets the loan period and any fee for late return.

## 7. Exceptions

7.1 Fines are waived for items due on a day the Libraries were closed by declaration of the University.
7.2 Graduate students writing a thesis or dissertation may request an extended loan of 120 days on standard items with the written approval of their advisor.

## 8. Appeals

Fine appeals must be submitted through the library account within **30 days** of the fine date. Decisions are issued within 10 business days and are final.

# Campus Parking

*Northgate State University · Transportation Services · Policy TS-1 · Version 7.1 · Supersedes TS-1 v7.0 · Responsible official: Director of Transportation Services*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy regulates the parking of motor vehicles on property owned or controlled by the University. It applies to students, employees, contractors and visitors. Operating a vehicle on campus constitutes acceptance of this policy.

## 2. Definitions

- **Permit:** a virtual permit linked to a registered licence plate. No physical permit is issued.
- **Enforcement hours:** **7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday**, excluding university holidays.
- **Calendar day:** every day, including weekends and holidays.
- **Reserved space:** a space signed for a named individual, a department, service vehicles or persons with disabilities.

## 3. Permits

3.1 A valid permit is required to park in any campus lot or garage during enforcement hours. Garages and reserved spaces are enforced at all times.
3.2 Permit types and annual prices:

| Permit | Eligibility | Annual price |
|---|---|---|
| Student Commuter | Students living off campus | $185 |
| Student Resident | Students in university housing | $240 |
| Graduate Garage | Graduate students and graduate assistants (Policy GS-4) | $420 |
| Faculty/Staff | Employees | $520 |
| Motorcycle | Any permit holder or applicant | $75 |

3.3 Up to **two vehicles** may be registered to one permit; only one may be on campus at a time.
3.4 Semester permits are sold at **45%** of the annual price. Permits are not transferable and are not refundable after the fourth week of the semester.

## 4. Citations

| Violation | Fine |
|---|---|
| No valid permit | $35 |
| Expired meter | $25 |
| Parking in a reserved space | $75 |
| Fire lane or blocking access | $150 |
| Disability space without placard | $250 |

4.1 Fines unpaid after **21 days** are charged to the student or employee account. Three or more unpaid citations result in a hold on registration and transcripts.
4.2 A vehicle with **five or more** unpaid citations may be immobilized or towed at the owner's expense.

## 5. Appeals

5.1 An appeal must be filed through the parking portal within **14 calendar days** of the citation date. The portal requires an NSU account (Policy IT-7).
5.2 A written decision is issued within 10 business days. A second-level appeal to the Parking Appeals Board may be filed within 7 days of that decision. The Board's decision is final.

## 6. Exceptions

6.1 The permit requirement is suspended during a declared weather emergency and on days the University is closed.
6.2 A first citation for "no valid permit" is voided if the owner purchases a permit within 3 business days.

## 7. Visitors

Visitor parking is available in the Union Garage at **$2 per hour**, up to $12 per day. Departments may request complimentary visitor codes for official guests.
